Message bodies now render in the proportional face at 15px with 1.6 line height, capped at about 90 characters per line, and the fallback keeps aligned text in monospace. Full suite passes serially (704 passed, 32 skipped) and `pnpm typecheck` is clean.

**Branch:** `reader-body-type-measure`, head `b00bf56` (no push, no PR)

## Files changed
- `src/assets/style.css`:
  - new tokens `--type-reading: 0.9375rem` and `--leading-reading: 1.6`;
  - `.message-body` is now `--font-ui` with the reading tokens and `max-width: 65ch`;
  - new `.message-body.message-body-mono` keeps the old mono values and uses `max-width: 88ch`.
- `src/components/ReaderView.vue`: one import and one `:class` binding.
- `src/lib/message-body-format.ts` (new): `bodyNeedsMonospace(bodyText)`.
- `tests/message-body-format.test.ts` (new): unit tests for the helper.

Message content is still text-interpolated with `pre-wrap` and `overflow-wrap: anywhere`. `--type-mono` is unchanged. Only `.message-body` used the mono tokens, so no other surface moved. No existing test needed changing.

## Monospace fallback
I chose automatic detection over a toggle. It needs no state, no keyboard shortcut and no palette command, so it can't conflict with the other branches editing `ReaderView.vue` and `App.vue`.

A body stays monospace if it has any of these:
- a line starting with `>`, after up to 3 spaces of indent;
- two consecutive lines with 4+ leading spaces, or a tab;
- two or more lines with at least two `|` each.

The text is never altered. The mono variant is capped at 88ch rather than 65ch, so emails hard-wrapped at 72–78 columns aren't soft-wrapped a second time.

The catch is that any reply with a `>` quote will render in mono, and a prose message can't be forced into mono. If you want that, a toggle can be added later.

## Measure (1280×800, default fixture)
- **Before:** mono 13.6px, 931px wide, about 114 characters per line.
- **After:** proportional 15px, 614px wide, left-aligned with the message header (both at x=58.4).
- **Long prose paragraph, after:** 89, 80, 84 and 94 characters on the full lines.
- **First attempt:** `80ch` gave about 110 characters per line. `ch` is the width of `0`, and average proportional glyphs are narrower, so I tightened it to 65ch.
- **Quoted fixture:** the mono fallback applied and measured 720px wide at 88ch.

## Evidence
Directory: `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-sofianebebert-workspace-worktrees-email-os-t3-8289bc5f/c76d33d1-bfb7-485b-a7f9-1da77be42a31/scratchpad/evidence/p2-body-type/`

- `after-1280x800.png`
- `after-long-prose-1280x800.png`
- `after-quoted-mono-fallback-1280x800.png`

The last two used a temporary fixture edit in `browser-fake.ts`, which I reverted and which is not in the commit. The dev server is stopped and the preview tab is closed.

## Tests
The first parallel full run had flaky timeout failures in app, account, stars and discovery tests, and the failing set changed between runs. Those files pass when run on their own, `tests/app.component.test.ts` passes on the base commit, and the serial full run is green.

## DESIGN.md notes (I did not edit it)
- **Tokens:** `--type-reading` 0.9375rem and `--leading-reading` 1.6 are new. `--type-mono` and `--leading-mono` stay, now only for the aligned-text fallback.
- **Typography:** "Label/Mono Font: ui-monospace, for plain-text message bodies only" becomes "message bodies use the UI face at the reading size; mono only for bodies with quotes, indented blocks or tables". The "Mono (400, 0.85rem, 1.45)" line should be reworded to match.
- **Item 14:** "Mono body" in the typeset-pass description is now outdated.
- **Item 16:** the "reader's type is on the shell scale" claim no longer holds, since the reader body adds a 15px step.
- **Standing constraint:** "safe literal plain text" is unchanged.

**Branch / head:** `reader-icon-header-actions` @ `ea406ed`, committed and not pushed.

**Files changed:** `src/components/ReaderView.vue`, `src/App.vue`, `src/components/HeaderGlyph.vue`, `src/assets/style.css`, `tests/app.component.test.ts`, `tests/drafts.component.test.ts`.

**What changed**
- **Header actions:** `ReaderView` teleports its icon buttons into two new host spans in the app header. It falls back to inline rendering when no host is passed, so standalone reader tests still find every `data-test` id.
- **Back arrow:** it leads the context title, with its glyph on the 50px inset.
- **Right-aligned icons:** Mark done / not done, read/unread toggle, Files and links, Prepare reply, then previous/next chevrons, then the existing palette and search glyphs.
- **Accessibility and test ids:** each icon has hidden text carrying the old label, plus a title with its shortcut. All `data-test` ids are kept.
- **Chevrons:** K/J use an `@move` emit, handled by the existing `moveReaderConversation`, and App computes availability from `resolveReaderNeighbor`. They are disabled at the ends of the list and hidden in Activity, Reminders and Trash readers, where J/K do nothing.
- **Reply sentence:** it is now the reply button's title and a visually-hidden `reply-source-label`, linked by `aria-describedby`. The blocked-reply notice is unchanged.
- **Text controls:** read state, "Mark read/unread" (unknown state) and the count-labelled bulk controls ("Mark N done", "Mark N read"…) stay as text. They sit in one `reader-meta-row` line under the subject, which renders only when there is something to show.
- **No layout shift:** the toolbar row and its rule are removed, and disabled buttons keep their 32px slot.
- **Tests:** I added a test for the header icons and the prev/next chevrons, and updated the "prepares a reply" test to find the button from the app root, since it is no longer inside the reader article.

**Checks beyond the suite:** I clicked through the thread in the preview (next, prev, done, back). At 1030px the trail fits (search glyph right edge 742 against header right 758). At 640px nothing overflows, and the document is no wider than the window. The fixture workspace has read controls off, so the read-toggle glyph was not exercised visually. Native tooltips don't appear in screenshots, so the tooltip shot shows the focus ring and brightened glyph instead.

**Evidence** (all in `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-sofianebebert-workspace-worktrees-email-os-t3-8289bc5f/c76d33d1-bfb7-485b-a7f9-1da77be42a31/scratchpad/evidence/p1-header-actions/`):
- `before-reader.png`
- `after-reader-1280.png`
- `after-reader-1030.png`
- `after-focus-hover-done.png`
- `after-flow-next-prev-done-back.mp4` (about 6 seconds: open, next, prev, next, done, back)

**Notes for the parent**
- **DESIGN.md:** the reader's actions now live in the split header, not a toolbar row. Reader actions are icon-only quiet glyphs (32px pitch, icon-muted, text-primary on hover/focus), each with a hidden text name and a title carrying its shortcut. Honest-state controls (read state, count-labelled bulk actions) stay as text under the subject. The existing `HeaderGlyph` stroke is 1.4px, not 1.5px, so I kept 1.4 for consistency.
- **Merge conflicts:** I touched the toolbar block and the subject/meta area in `ReaderView.vue`, and added two spans and four props in `App.vue`. Merging with the star status line and collapsed-snippet branches should conflict only near the subject.

**Not done:** there is no remind (clock) icon in the reader actions. The existing Reminders glyph in the header trail already covers it. Prev/next and K/J use `title` strings that I did not add to `browsingActions`, because that list feeds the command palette.
